points.description: States that summing or averaging (smoothing/combining) a random series/data can produce an effect, i.e. the operation of summation or averaging on random data is the cause.
points.partial_credit: Half if only vaguely mentions processing/manipulating data without naming summation or averaging.

points.description: States that this generates oscillations/cyclic movements (apparent periodicity) that were not present in the original data.
points.partial_credit: Half if oscillations/cycles are mentioned but not that they are absent from the original data.

rubric.notes: Full marks (2) for saying that summing or averaging a random series creates oscillations or cycles that are not in the original data; any wording or clear synonyms are fine. Give 1 mark if only one of the two ideas is clearly stated, or both are stated vaguely or with a minor error. Give 0 for wrong or unrelated definitions.
